summary: Source decomposition from five primary sources read directly: Herr, Sur la cohomologie galoisienne des corps p-adiques (BSMF 126, 1998) - the introduction, Sec. 1.1-1.2, all of Sec. 2, Sec. 3.1-3.3 and Sec. 4; Cherbonnier-Colmez, Representations p-adiques surconvergentes - Sec. I.1-I.3, II.1-II.4, the statement of III.1.1 and all of III.5; Kedlaya-Pottharst-Xiao, Cohomology of arithmetic families of (phi,Gamma)-modules - Sec. 1, 2.2, 2.3, 4.2 and 4.4; Berger, Limites de representations cristallines - Sec. 2.1 and 4.1-4.2; and LLZ, Wach modules and Iwasawa theory for modular forms - Sec. 2.2. Four points are recorded against the stage texts. (1) TOWER CONVENTIONS DIFFER AND ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE: Herr takes K_infinity to be the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, so Gamma_K is torsion-free and no Delta-invariants appear anywhere in his paper; Cherbonnier-Colmez take K_infinity = K(mu_{p^infinity}); and KPX define Delta_K to be the p-TORSION subgroup of Gamma_K, trivial for p odd, not the prime-to-p torsion named in the PG.3 stage text. (2) HERR 1998 DOES NOT PROVE TATE DUALITY: his introduction defers Theorem C to a later publication, so PG.3's duality requirement cannot be sourced to this paper; the rational Robba-coefficient duality is available from Liu via KPX Thm. 2.3.11 and Thm. 4.4.5(3). (3) THE psi INTEGRALITY IS A THEOREM, NOT A DEFINITION: Herr Sec. 3.1.1 proves Tr_{E^nr/sigma(E^nr)}(O_{E^nr}) is contained in p sigma(O_{E^nr}) from the degree-p purely inseparable residual extension, which is exactly what PG.4 demands. (4) THE psi-COMPLEX COMPARISON RESTS ON BIJECTIVITY OF gamma - 1 ON Ker psi (Herr Thm. 3.8), which in turn rests on the fundamental Lemma 3.9 proved in Sec. 5 under the hypothesis that K_infinity/K is totally ramified. Fontaine's equivalence, Tate duality integrally, the chain-level comparison with Galois cochains, the integral Iwasawa comparison H^1_Iw = D(T)^{psi=1} (Cherbonnier-Colmez 1999), Wach's original theorem, and the proof of the KPX main theorem are all recorded as gaps with next source actions. All eight stages are partial; none is source_decomposed. [Corrected in review REVIEW-EXT-08-EXT-16. Point (4) needs a qualification. Herr's Theorem 3.8 is proved for EVERY K: its proof (Sec. 3.3.4, printed pp. 585-589) first replaces K by a finite unramified Galois extension and then assumes K_infinity/K totally ramified. The total-ramification hypothesis of Lemma 3.9 is therefore NOT inherited by Theorem 3.8, by Proposition 4.1 or by the psi-complex comparison. Further corrections: Herr's Theorem 4.3 has H^i(gr^0) = H^{i-1}(Gamma_K, M/(psi-1)M), with the degree shift; Herr Prop. 3.2(5) is M_nil = direct sum over i of phi^i(Ker psi), not O_E(K) tensor Ker psi; the KPX change-of-generator map has three components; LLZ's lattice list does not repeat triviality mod pi; Berger's Prop. 4.4 divisibility step needs p odd as written; several page locators were off by one. All five library hashes match.]

nodes.title: Fr R, the field of norms of the cyclotomic tower, and the G_K-equivariant embedding
nodes.statement: Let C be the p-adic completion of an algebraic closure of K and Fr R the set of sequences (x^{(n)}) in C with (x^{(n+1)})^p = x^{(n)}, with multiplication componentwise and addition by the limit of (x^{(n+m)}+y^{(n+m)})^{p^m}. Then Fr R is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, complete for v(x) = v_C(x^{(0)}), with residue field k. For L/K_infinity finite, the field of norms E_K(L) = inverse limit over finite subextensions T/K of L under norm maps is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic p with residue field that of L, the construction is functorial, and passing to the inductive limit gives an equivalence between the category of algebraic extensions of K_infinity and that of separable extensions of E_K(K_infinity). There is a continuous G_K-equivariant embedding j_K of E_K(Kbar) into Fr R, and it identifies Gal(E_K(Kbar)/E_K(K_infinity)) with Gal(Kbar/K_infinity).
hypotheses: K_infinity is the CYCLOTOMIC Z_p-EXTENSION of K contained in Kbar in Herr's convention (Sec. 1.1.1.2), not K(mu_{p^infinity}); consequently Gamma_K = Gal(K_infinity/K) is isomorphic to Z_p and has no torsion
The residue field k_infinity of K_infinity is a finite extension of k
Addition in Fr R is defined by a limit that must be shown to exist; multiplication is componentwise
The embedding j_K is built from convergence of the family of norms along the filter of sections of the tamely ramified layers, for each r in N separately
The whole construction rests on Wintenberger's field-of-norms theory, which Herr cites as [Win] and does not reprove
proofSteps: Define Fr R with the two operations and verify it is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, complete for v(x) = v_C(x^{(0)}), whose residue field is identified with k by x -> ([x]^{1/p^n})_n.

Define E_K(L) as the inverse limit of the finite subextensions under the norm maps, with the componentwise product and the limit-of-sums addition; verify the valuation V(x) = v_C(x_K) makes it complete discretely valued.

Use functoriality and the inductive limit over finite extensions of K_infinity to get E_K(Kbar) as a separable closure of E_K(K_infinity), with G_K acting continuously and E_K(L) = E_K(Kbar)^{Gal(Kbar/L)}.
Construct j_K: for x in E_K(L), the family of p^r-th roots of the norms along S_r(L) converges to j_K(x)^{(r)} in C; collect these into an element of Fr R.
acceptance: Check that E_0, E_K and E^sep embed in Fr R and are identified with the images of E_{K_0}((K_0)_infinity), E_K(K_infinity) and E_K(Kbar) (Herr printed p. 570). Check the independence from the choice of the compatible system e of p-power roots of unity that Herr records

nodes.title: The rings Etilde, E_F, E_K, Atilde, A_K and their phi and Gamma_K actions
nodes.statement: Let k_F be perfect of characteristic p, O_F = W(k_F), F = O_F[1/p], and fix an algebraic closure Fbar. For K/F finite put K_n = K(mu_{p^n}), K_infinity the union, H_K = ker(chi restricted to G_K) = Gal(Fbar/K_infinity), Gamma_K = G_K/H_K = Gal(K_infinity/K). Let Etilde be the tilt of the completion of Fbar, a complete algebraically closed field of characteristic p with v_E(x) = v_p(x^{(0)}); choose eps = (1, eps^{(1)}, ...) with eps^{(1)} not 1, so that v_E(eps - 1) = p/(p-1), and set E_F = k_F((eps-1)) inside Etilde, E the separable closure of E_F in Etilde, E_K = E^{H_K}, EtildeK = Etilde^{H_K}. Then E_K/E_F is finite separable of degree [K_infinity : F_infinity] and EtildeK is the completed perfection of E_K. Let Atilde = W(Etilde), Btilde = Atilde[1/p], A = B intersect Atilde with B the completion of the maximal unramified extension of B_F inside Btilde.
hypotheses: k_F is perfect of characteristic p; F is absolutely unramified. K is a finite extension of F inside Fbar
In THIS convention K_infinity = K(mu_{p^infinity}), so Gamma_K is an open subgroup of Z_p^x and in general has torsion; this differs from Herr's cyclotomic Z_p-extension convention
The choice of eps is a choice of compatible system of primitive p^n-th roots of unity; the normalization v_E(eps-1) = p/(p-1) depends on v_p(p) = 1
The field-of-norms theory is used to identify Gal(E/E_F) with H_F
proofSteps: Build Etilde as the set of p-power-compatible sequences in the completion of Fbar with the standard two operations, and verify v_E is a valuation for which Etilde is complete and algebraically closed.
Fix eps and compute v_E(eps-1) = p/(p-1); define E_F = k_F((eps-1)).
Take E the separable closure of E_F inside Etilde; the field-of-norms theory identifies Gal(E/E_F) with H_F, and E_K = E^{H_K} has degree [K_infinity : F_infinity] over E_F.
Pass to Witt vectors: Atilde = W(Etilde), Btilde = Frac(Atilde), and cut out A and B by intersecting with the completion of the maximal unramified extension of B_F.
acceptance: Over F = Q_p compute phi(pi) = (1+pi)^p - 1 and gamma(pi) = (1+pi)^{chi(gamma)} - 1 for pi = [eps]-1
Check the degree formula [E_K : E_F] = [K_infinity : F_infinity] on a ramified quadratic extension

Check that the two tower conventions (Herr's Z_p-extension and this one) give E_K differing by the torsion layer of Gal(K(mu_{p^infinity})/K). That layer is prime to p for p odd, but has order 2 for p = 2. Herr builds E_0 as the Gamma_tor-invariants of the mu_{p^infinity} field (printed p. 569).

nodes.title: One cannot in general choose a lift t of a uniformizer with W(k_infinity)[[t]] stable under both Gamma_K and sigma
nodes.statement: For every g in G_K, g(pi_0)/pi_0 is a unit of W[[pi_0]]; and if K_infinity/K is totally ramified and pi is a uniformizer of E_K, then g(pi)/pi is a fundamental unit of E_K, i.e. an integral element congruent to 1 modulo the maximal ideal. However, if t is a lift in O_{E(K)} of a uniformizer of E_K, it is in general NOT possible to choose t so that W(k_infinity)[[t]] is stable under both the Gamma_K-action and sigma; such a choice is possible when d_K = [k_infinity : k], that is when K is contained in an unramified extension of (K_0)_infinity, and then t = pi_0 works.
hypotheses: The first assertion uses Fontaine's map theta : W(R) -> O_C and the fact that the kernel of its restriction to W[[pi_0]] is generated by pi_0, together with G_K-equivariance of theta
The second assertion uses that K_infinity/K totally ramified makes the residue field of E_K equal to k, on which G_K acts trivially

The impossibility argument is by contradiction and imports Wach's theorem [Wac, Sec. A.5] that a representation of finite height becomes crystalline over some (K_0)_n; it is not self-contained in Herr
proofSteps: Lemma 1.1, first part: theta restricted to W[[pi_0]] has kernel (pi_0); since theta is G_K-equivariant, pi_0 and g(pi_0) generate the same ideal of W[[pi_0]], so the ratio is a unit.
Second part: when K_infinity/K is totally ramified the residue field of E_K is k with trivial G_K-action, so g(pi)/pi reduces to 1.

Obstruction: if W(k_infinity)[[t]] were stable under both actions, the representation induced from K to K_0 of the trivial representation would be of finite height, hence crystalline over some (K_0)_n by Wach, forcing K unramified over (K_0)_n.

Exhibit a ramified K where no such t exists, using the criterion d_K = [k_infinity : k]
Check the theta-kernel computation

nodes.title: D_K and V_K are quasi-inverse equivalences between p-torsion representations and torsion etale phi-Gamma-modules
nodes.statement: For V a p-torsion representation of G_K put D_K(V) = (O_{Ehat^nr} tensor_{Z_p} V)^{G_{E_K}}, with the Gamma_K = G_K/G_{E_K} action and the phi induced by the Frobenius sigma; this is a torsion etale phi-Gamma_K-module over O_{E(K)}. Conversely V_K(M) = (O_{Ehat^nr} tensor_{O_{E(K)}} M)^{phi = 1}. Both functors are additive and exact, and D_K is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse V_K. Moreover the Z_p elementary divisors of V coincide with those of D_K(V) over O_{E(K)} up to units.
hypotheses: 'etale of torsion' means: of finite length as an O_{E(K)}-module AND generated by the image of phi. Finite length alone is not enough
A phi-Gamma-module is an O_{E(K)}-module with a sigma-semilinear phi and a CONTINUOUS Gamma-semilinear action of Gamma commuting with phi; continuity is part of the data
Gamma here is Gal(K_infinity/K) for K_infinity the cyclotomic Z_p-extension (Herr's convention)
Herr states this as Theorem 1.2 quoting Fontaine [Fo1, A.1.2.4-A.1.2.6]; no proof is given in Herr
proofSteps: Quoted: Herr Theorem 1.2 attributes the equivalence to Fontaine, Representations p-adiques des corps locaux I, Grothendieck Festschrift, Sections A.1.2.4-A.1.2.6.
What Herr does prove and use downstream: the etale lattice statement of Proposition 2.4(1), which supplies the phi-linearization the stage insists on.
acceptance: Compute D_K for an unramified character and for Z/p(1)
Check exactness on a short exact sequence of p-torsion representations
Check the elementary divisor statement on Z/p^2

De plus, les facteurs invariants sur Z_p d'une representation de p-torsion V de G_K coincident avec ceux de D_K(V) sur O_{E(K)} (a des unites pres).

nodes.title: Every torsion phi-Gamma-module contains a phi- and Gamma-stable lattice on which phi - 1 is bijective
nodes.statement: Let M be a phi-Gamma_K-module over O_{E(K)} of finite length as an O_{E_0}-module. Then (1) M contains a pi_0-lattice (a finitely generated W[[pi_0]]-submodule generating M over W((pi_0))) that is stable under phi and Gamma_K and on which phi - 1 is bijective; and (2) for every x in M there exist r in N and y in M with (gamma-1)^r(x) = (phi-1)(y).
hypotheses: M is killed by a power of p, so it can be regarded as a finite length W((pi_0))-module

The construction of the lattice needs an integer s with the matrix entries of phi in pi_0^{-s} W[[pi_0]] + p W((pi_0)), and then r with p^{n-1}(p-1)r > s where p^n kills M; these explicit inequalities are used to force phi-contraction
Bijectivity of phi - 1 on the lattice comes from phi^r(x) -> 0 for x in the lattice, so that the Neumann series for (phi-1)^{-1} converges
proofSteps: Choose generators e_i of M over W((pi_0)) and write phi(e_i) = sum_j a_{ij} e_j.
Pick s with all a_{ij} in pi_0^{-s} W[[pi_0]] + p W((pi_0)) and r with p^{n-1}(p-1) r > s; using sigma(pi_0) = pi_0^p mod p one gets sigma^{p^{n-1} r}(pi_0) = pi_0^{p^{...}} mod p^n.
Set f_i = pi_0^{p^{...} r} e_i and let R be the W[[pi_0]]-module they generate; the displayed congruence shows R is phi-stable, and the f_i generate M over W((pi_0)), so R is a lattice.

nodes.title: The rings A^{dagger,r} and the definition of an overconvergent representation
nodes.statement: For r in R_+ let Atilde^{dagger,r} be the subring of Atilde = W(Etilde) of x = sum p^k [x_k] with w_k(x) + (pr/(p-1)) k bounded below and tending to infinity, Atilde^dagger the union over r, and A^{dagger,r} = A intersect Atilde^{dagger,r}. Atilde^{dagger,r} is closed in Atilde and complete for the alpha-adic topology for suitable alpha, and Btilde^dagger is a field stable under G_F and phi. For V a Z_p- or p-adic representation of G_K set D^dagger(V) = (A^dagger tensor_{Z_p} V)^{H_K} and D_r^dagger(V) = (A_r^dagger tensor_{Z_p} V)^{H_K}. Then dim_{B_K^dagger} D^dagger(V) <= dim_{Q_p} V, and V is called OVERCONVERGENT when equality holds, equivalently when D_r^dagger(V) contains a B_K-basis of D(V) for r large enough.

nodes.title: Every p-adic representation of G_K is overconvergent
nodes.statement: Let k_F be perfect of characteristic p, F = W(k_F)[1/p] and K a finite extension of F. Then every p-adic representation of G_K is overconvergent: for V of dimension d there exists M in GL_d(B^dagger) such that the cocycle sigma -> M^{-1} U_sigma sigma(M) is trivial on H_K and takes values in GL_d(B_K^dagger); the columns of M form a basis of D(V) consisting of overconvergent elements.

The engine is Theorem III.1.1: the maps H^1(Gamma_K, GL_d(phi^{-infinity}(B_K^dagger))) -> H^1(Gamma_K, GL_d(BtildeK^dagger)) -> H^1(G_K, GL_d(Btilde^dagger)) induced by inflation and inclusion are BIJECTIONS

nodes.title: Induction stability, the psi = 1 criterion, and invertibility of gamma - 1 on D^dagger(V)^{psi=0}
nodes.statement: (i) The category of overconvergent representations of G_K is stable under induction: for L/K finite and V a p-adic representation of G_K, V is overconvergent iff it is overconvergent as a representation of G_L. (ii) V is overconvergent if and only if D(V)^{psi=1} consists of overconvergent elements, i.e. is contained in D^dagger(V). (iii) If V is overconvergent and gamma_K generates Gamma_K then gamma_K - 1 admits a continuous inverse on D^dagger(V)^{psi=0}. (iv) The category is stable under extension and contains the abelian representations. The underlying ring statement is that B_L^dagger/B_K^dagger is an extension of degree [L_infinity : K_infinity], Galois with group Gal(L_infinity/K_infinity) when L/K is Galois.
hypotheses: In (iii) gamma_K must be a topological generator of Gamma_K; at p = 2 Gamma_K has torsion and one must pass to a torsion-free subgroup first
The degree statement [B_L^dagger : B_K^dagger] = [L_infinity : K_infinity] uses that Tr_{K_infinity/F_infinity}(B_K^dagger) is contained in B_F^dagger and a quadratic-form argument on Tr(x^2)
Lemma II.4.2 requires the discriminant of the monic polynomial to be PRIME TO p; that is what makes the generated extension of B unramified
Cherbonnier-Colmez reproduce the proofs of (i) and (iii) only; (ii) and (iv) are quoted from Cherbonnier's thesis [2], which is not in the supplied library
proofSteps: (i) Reduce by Hilbert 90 to Proposition II.4.1: the natural map B_F tensor_{B_F^dagger} B_K^dagger -> B_K is bijective. Injectivity uses the trace form; surjectivity uses Lemma II.4.2.

Lemma II.4.2: if P in A^dagger[X] is monic with discriminant prime to p, the extension of B generated by a root is unramified hence equals B, so the roots lie in A; one then checks they also lie in Atilde^dagger.
(iii) is proved in Sec. II.5-II.6 by reducing to the trivial representation of G_F, which the authors state shortens the devissage of [2].

nodes.title: The three-term complex C_{phi,gamma}(D_K(V)) computes H^*(G_K, V)
nodes.statement: Fix a topological generator gamma of Gamma_K and set tau = gamma - 1, rho = phi - 1. For V a p-torsion representation of G_K and every i, H^i(G_K, V) is isomorphic to the i-th cohomology group of the complex (first term in degree -1) 0 -> D_K(V) -> D_K(V) + D_K(V) -> D_K(V) -> 0, with x -> (rho(x), tau(x)) and (y,z) -> tau(y) - rho(z). In particular H^i(G_K,V) = 0 for i >= 3, which reproves Theorem A.
hypotheses: V is a p-TORSION representation; the Z_p- and Q_p-coefficient statements are obtained afterwards by a Mittag-Leffler argument that uses the finiteness Theorem B, and the finiteness needs k finite
Gamma_K = Gal(K_infinity/K) with K_infinity the cyclotomic Z_p-EXTENSION, hence procyclic; a topological generator gamma exists and no Delta-invariants appear
The proof needs the ind-etale category PhiGammaM^{ind-et,p-tor}, which HAS enough injectives, unlike the category of torsion etale objects
Effaceability is proved in degrees 1 and 2 only; degree 0 agrees with Galois cohomology by construction
proofSteps: Extend D_K to an equivalence between discrete p-torsion G_K-modules and ind-etale phi-Gamma_K-modules; the functor V -> V^{G_K} corresponds to M -> M^{phi=1, gamma=1}.
The functor C_{phi,gamma} from the ind-etale category to complexes of abelian groups is additive, exact and faithful, so (H^i = H_i o C_{phi,gamma}) is a cohomological functor.
Since it agrees with Galois cohomology in degree 0, it suffices to prove effaceability in higher degrees (Herr cites [Poi, cor. p. 65]).
Lemma 2.2: any object M of the ind-etale category embeds, for a given x in M, in a torsion etale N_x with x in rho(N_x); this is deduced from Proposition 2.4(2).

Degree 2 effaceability is immediate from Lemma 2.2. Degree 1: given tau(y) = rho(z), embed M in N_y with rho(x) = y, then adjoin a free rank-one summand O_{E(K)}/p^s generated by v with phi(v) = v and gamma(v) = v + tau(x) - z; then y = rho(x-v) and z = tau(x-v), so (y,z) dies.

nodes.title: Which torsion subgroup is inverted, and where p = 2 actually bites
nodes.statement: Three conventions appear in the literature and must not be conflated. (a) Herr takes K_infinity to be the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, so Gamma_K is isomorphic to Z_p, procyclic and torsion-free, and the Herr complex is formed on D itself. (b) Cherbonnier-Colmez take K_infinity = K(mu_{p^infinity}), so Gamma_K is an open subgroup of Z_p^x with a finite torsion subgroup; with Z_p-coefficients one forms the complex on D^Delta for Delta the prime-to-p torsion, and exactness of Delta-invariants uses that |Delta| is invertible. [Attribution corrected in review: Cherbonnier-Colmez fix the tower and Gamma_K but form no Herr complex in the sections read. The D^Delta formulation is the atlas PG.3 stage's ('For odd p and the finite prime-to-p torsion subgroup'), not a Cherbonnier-Colmez statement.] (c) KPX, working with Q_p-affinoid coefficients, define Delta_K to be the p-TORSION subgroup of Gamma_K, which is trivial for p not equal to 2 and at largest cyclic of order 2, and form the complex on M^{Delta_K}. In all three the point of the quotient is that Gamma_K/Delta_K must be procyclic. At p = 2 the torsion subgroup contains p-torsion, so taking invariants is not exact on Z_2-modules and the naive complex is wrong.
hypotheses: In convention (b) exactness of Delta-invariants requires |Delta| prime to p; with Z_p-coefficients this fails precisely at p = 2
In convention (c) the coefficients are Q_p-affinoid, so prime-to-p torsion invariants are automatically exact and only p-torsion has to be removed
Convention (a) has no torsion at all, but its coefficient ring E_K is that of the Z_p-extension, which is a proper subfield of the one attached to K(mu_{p^infinity})
proofSteps: Record Herr's tower convention from Sec. 1.1.1.2 and observe Gamma_K is isomorphic to Z_p.
Record Cherbonnier-Colmez's convention from Sec. I.1 and observe Gamma_K is an open subgroup of Z_p^x.

Conclude that a statement quoted from one convention cannot be transported to another without comparing the coefficient rings E_K.

nodes.title: The canonical three-step filtration of the Herr complex and the finiteness/Euler characteristic theorem
nodes.statement: Filter C(M) = C_{psi,gamma}(M) by C^0 = C, C^1 the subcomplex 0 -> M^{psi=1} -> M^{psi=1} -> 0 -> 0, C^2 the subcomplex 0 -> M^{phi=1} -> M^{phi=1} -> 0 -> 0, C^3 = 0. Then H^i(gr^0 C(M)) = H^{i-1}(Gamma_K, M/(psi-1)M) [degree shift restored in review from a render of Herr printed p. 592]; H^i(gr^1 C(M)) = 0 except H^1(gr^1 C(M)) = c(M)/tau(c(M)) where c(M) = (phi-1)M intersect Ker psi; and H^i(gr^2 C(M)) = H^i(Gamma_K, M^{phi=1}) = H^i(Gamma_K, V^{Gal(Kbar/K_infinity)}). This yields a three-step filtration of H^i(M) and, for K/Q_p finite, the finiteness of all H^i and the Euler characteristic formula of Theorem B.
hypotheses: For the finiteness conclusions K/Q_p must be finite (so k is finite and W is finite over Z_p); Proposition 3.6(2) is stated with that hypothesis
The identification H^1(gr^1) = c(M)/tau(c(M)) uses that phi - 1 induces a Gamma_K-equivariant isomorphism M^{psi=1}/M^{phi=1} onto c(M) and that tau acts injectively on Ker psi
The order of c(M)/tau(c(M)) is p^{[K:Q_p] l_V} by Corollary 3.11, whose proof uses Lemma 3.12 on Z_p((X))-modules and Theorem 3.8 on the structure of Ker psi

Theorem 3.8 rests on the 'fundamental lemma' 3.9 (proof in Sec. 5), which assumes K_infinity/K totally ramified. Theorem 3.8 itself is proved for every K: the proof (Sec. 3.3.4, printed pp. 585-589) first replaces K by a finite unramified Galois extension and then assumes K_infinity/K and L/K totally ramified. So no total-ramification hypothesis attaches to Theorem 3.8 or to Theorem B. [Corrected in review.]
proofSteps: Build the three-step filtration and identify the graded pieces; gr^2 is immediate from M^{phi=1} = V^{H_K}.

Lemma 4.2: gr^0 C(M) is quasi-isomorphic to 0 -> 0 -> M/(psi-1)M -> M/(psi-1)M -> 0 (first term in degree -1, so the two copies sit in degrees 1 and 2, which is the source of the shift H^{i-1}), because psi - 1 induces a bijection M/M^{psi=1} -> (psi-1)M.
For gr^1, use that phi - 1 maps M^{psi=1}/M^{phi=1} isomorphically onto (phi-1)M intersect Ker psi = c(M), and that tau is injective on Ker psi.
Assemble the long exact sequences; finiteness of V^{Gal(Kbar/K_infinity)}, of M/(psi-1)M (Proposition 3.6(2), K/Q_p finite) and of c(M)/tau(c(M)) (Corollary 3.11) gives Theorem B.

nodes.title: Construction of psi on O_{E^nr} and the p-divisibility of the trace
nodes.statement: The extension E^nr / sigma(E^nr) has degree p and its residual extension is purely inseparable of degree p; consequently Tr_{E^nr/sigma(E^nr)}(O_{E^nr}) is contained in p sigma(O_{E^nr}). Since sigma is injective one may therefore define psi : O_{E^nr} -> O_{E^nr} by psi(x) = (1/p) sigma^{-1}(Tr_{E^nr/sigma(E^nr)}(x)). It is an additive G_K-equivariant map with psi(a sigma(b)) = b psi(a) and psi(1) = 1, and it restricts to O_{E(K)} commuting with Gamma_K.
hypotheses: The division by p is legitimate ONLY because the trace image is contained in p sigma(O_{E^nr}); that inclusion is what the degree-p purely inseparable residual extension buys, and it must be proved rather than assumed
sigma must be injective for sigma^{-1} to make sense on the trace image
The restriction to O_{E(K)} is obtained by taking G_{E_K}-invariants, which is why psi commutes with Gamma_K
proofSteps: Compute the degree of E^nr over sigma(E^nr) and of the residual extension; both are p and the residual one is purely inseparable.

Deduce Tr(O_{E^nr}) in p sigma(O_{E^nr}): the trace of the residue extension is zero because it is purely inseparable of degree p, so the trace lands in the maximal ideal, and the sharper p-divisibility follows from the degree computation.
Define psi by the displayed formula and verify additivity, G_K-equivariance, psi(a sigma(b)) = b psi(a) and psi(1) = 1 from the projection formula for traces.
Restrict to G_{E_K}-invariants to get psi on O_{E(K)} commuting with Gamma_K.

nodes.title: The unique additive psi on a torsion etale phi-Gamma-module, with its identities
nodes.statement: Let M be a torsion etale phi-Gamma_K-module over O_{E(K)}. There is a UNIQUE additive map psi_M : M -> M with psi_M(a phi_M(x)) = psi(a) x for all a in O_{E(K)} and x in M. It is surjective, satisfies psi_M o phi_M = id_M and psi_M(phi(a) x) = a psi_M(x), and it commutes with Gamma_K.
hypotheses: Uniqueness uses ETALENESS: M is generated as an O_{E(K)}-module by the image of phi_M, so the defining identity determines psi_M
Existence is obtained by transporting psi tensor id_V through the equivalence of PG.1, i.e. it depends on Fontaine's theorem
psi_M is only a LEFT inverse of phi_M; phi_M psi_M is a projector, not the identity
proofSteps: Uniqueness: M is generated over O_{E(K)} by phi_M(M), so any additive map satisfying the identity is determined on generators.
Existence: use V_K to write M = D_K(V) with phi_M the restriction of sigma tensor id_V; then psi_{O_{E^nr}} tensor id_V descends to M and satisfies the identity.
The remaining identities psi_M phi_M = id and psi_M(phi(a)x) = a psi_M(x) follow from psi(a sigma(b)) = b psi(a) and psi(1) = 1.

nodes.title: Continuity of psi, the decomposition M = Ker psi + phi(M), and the length of Ker psi
nodes.statement: Let M be an etale phi-Gamma_K-module over O_{E(K)} killed by p^n, V = V_K(M) and l_V = long_{Z_p}(V). Then (1) psi is continuous; (2) for every r >= 1, Ker(psi^r) is a sigma^r(O_{E(K)})-submodule of M of finite length (p^r - 1) l_V, stable under Gamma_K, and M = Ker psi + phi(M) with Ker(psi^r) = the direct sum of phi^i(Ker psi) for 0 <= i <= r-1, the map (Ker psi)^r -> Ker(psi^r) being a Gamma_K-equivariant isomorphism; (3) psi(x) is the unique y with x - phi(y) in Ker psi; (4) the natural map Ker psi -> M/phi(M) is a sigma(O_{E(K)})-linear Gamma_K-equivariant homeomorphism; (5) the map from the direct sum over i in N of copies of Ker psi to the set M_nil of psi-nilpotent elements, sending an almost-zero sequence (a_i) to sum_i phi^i(a_i), is a group isomorphism commuting with Gamma_K. [Corrected in review from a render of printed p. 579: the earlier text read this as 'the image of O_{E(K)} tensor Ker psi'.] Moreover tau = gamma - 1 acts BIJECTIVELY on Ker psi, which is a W((tau))-module of finite length e_K l_V where e_K is the absolute ramification index of K.
hypotheses: M must be etale and of finite length; the length formulas use l_V = long_{Z_p}(V) and the absolute ramification index e_K
The directness of M = Ker(psi^r) + phi^r(M) (Herr prints the general r) uses that phi^r(x) in Ker(psi^r) forces x = psi^r(phi^r(x)) = 0.

The bijectivity of tau on Ker psi (Theorem 3.8) is NOT formal. Its proof uses the 'fundamental lemma' 3.9, proved in Herr Sec. 5 by ramification computations for a totally ramified Z_p-extension, and it imports Serre, Corps locaux (cor. 4 and cor. 1 p. 75, th. 2 p. 146). Theorem 3.8 itself holds for every K: Sec. 3.3.4 step 1 reduces to a finite unramified extension over which K_infinity/K is totally ramified. [Corrected in review.]
Statement (2) identifies Ker psi as a module over sigma^r(O_{E(K)}), not over O_{E(K)}
proofSteps: Continuity is immediate from the definition.
From psi(phi(a)x) = a psi(x) one gets by induction that Ker(psi^r) is a sigma^r(O_{E(K)})-submodule; finiteness of length follows because O_{E(K)} is finite over sigma^r(O_{E(K)}).
For x in M, x - phi(psi(x)) lies in Ker psi, so M = phi(M) + Ker psi; the sum is direct because psi(phi(x)) in Ker(psi^r) forces phi^r(x) = 0.
Induct to get Ker(psi^r) as the direct sum of the phi^i(Ker psi), checking directness by applying psi^m.
Length count: long_{sigma^r(O)}(M) = p^r long_O(M) and long_{sigma^r(O)}(phi^r(M)) = long_O(M), so Ker(psi^r) has length (p^r - 1) l_V.
Theorem 3.8 then upgrades Ker psi to a W((tau))-module of length e_K l_V on which tau is bijective, using Lemma 3.9.

Then the morphism of complexes given by 0, id, f, -psi, 0 from C_{phi,gamma}(M) to C_{psi,gamma}(M) is a QUASI-ISOMORPHISM.

That subcomplex has differential tau on Ker psi; bijectivity of tau on Ker psi (Theorem 3.8) makes it acyclic.
A surjection of complexes with acyclic kernel is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: The two-term psi-complex in degrees 1 and 2 and its identification with the Herr complex of the cyclotomic deformation
nodes.statement: For a (phi,Gamma_K)-module M over the relative Robba ring R_A(pi_K), define C_psi(M) = [M -> M] with differential psi - 1, concentrated in DEGREES 1 AND 2; its cohomology H^*_psi(M) is the Iwasawa cohomology, a module over R_A^infinity(Gamma_K). Let Dfm(M) be the cyclotomic deformation of M. Then there is a natural quasi-isomorphism C_{psi,gamma_K}(Dfm(M)) -> C_psi(M) of complexes of R_A^infinity(Gamma_K)-modules, and consequently an Iwasawa duality quasi-isomorphism C_psi(M^*) -> RHom_{R_A^infinity(Gamma_K)}(C_psi(M), R_A^infinity(Gamma_K)^iota)[-2]. Specializing at a continuous character eta of Gamma_K gives C_psi(M) derived-tensored over R_A^infinity(Gamma_K) with the residue field quasi-isomorphic to C_{psi,gamma_K}(M tensor L(eta^{-1})).

The iota-twist on R_A^infinity(Gamma_K) in the duality statement is the inversion involution on Gamma_K and must not be dropped

Its proof uses Shapiro's lemma, Pottharst [42, Theorem 1.6], KPX Theorem 2.3.7 and Theorem 4.4.8. nodes.title: Wach's criterion and the uniqueness of the Wach module
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p, F = Frac(W(k)) and Gamma_F = Gal(F(mu_{p^infinity})/F). Wach's theorem: a representation V of G_F of finite height is crystalline POSITIVE if and only if there exists a free B_F^+-submodule N of D^+(V) of rank d = dim V, stable under Gamma_F, such that the action of Gamma_F is trivial on N/pi N. Berger's refinement: one may arrange pi^s D^+(V) contained in N contained in D^+(V) for some integer s, and such an N is then UNIQUE, and in particular automatically phi-stable.
hypotheses: F must be ABSOLUTELY UNRAMIFIED (F = Frac(W(k)) with k perfect); Berger's paper is explicitly the 'non-ramified case' of Fontaine's conjecture and does not cover ramified K
V must be of finite height for Wach's criterion to apply; for V crystalline positive this is supplied by a theorem of Colmez
'Positive' means the Hodge-Tate weights lie in [-r, 0] after the twist Berger normalizes; the twist relating this to the convention HT(Q_p(1)) = 1 must be stated
Uniqueness holds only under the bracketing pi^s D^+(V) contained in N contained in D^+(V); without it N is not unique
proofSteps: Wach's theorem is quoted by Berger from [Wac, p. 380]; Berger does not reprove it.
Colmez's theorem gives that a crystalline positive V is of finite height, hence produces some N as in Wach's criterion.

Lemma 2.2: one may shrink/enlarge N to satisfy pi^s D^+(V) contained in N contained in D^+(V); uniqueness then follows from a Gamma_F-action argument, and phi-stability is a consequence rather than a hypothesis.
acceptance: Check the criterion on the trivial representation and on Q_p(1)
Check that dropping the bracketing pi^s D^+(V) in N destroys uniqueness

nodes.title: The three defining conditions of N(V), the lattice bijection, and N(V)/pi N(V) = D_cris(V)
nodes.statement: Let E be a finite extension of Q_p and V an E-linear representation of G_{Q_p}. Then V is crystalline with Hodge-Tate weights in [a,b] if and only if there exists a (necessarily unique) E tensor_{Q_p} B^+_{Q_p}-submodule N(V) of D(V) such that (1) N(V) is free of rank d = dim_E V; (2) the Gamma-action preserves N(V) and is trivial on N(V)/pi N(V); (3) phi(pi^b N(V)) is contained in pi^b N(V) and pi^b N(V)/phi^*(pi^b N(V)) is killed by q^{b-a}, where q = phi(pi)/pi. If V is crystalline and positive one may take b = 0, phi preserves N(V), and with Fil^i N(V) = {x : phi(x) in q^i N(V)} the quotient N(V)/pi N(V) is a filtered phi-module isomorphic to D_cris(V). For a G-stable lattice T, N(T) = N(V) intersect D(T) and T -> N(T) is a bijection between G-stable lattices in V and the O_E tensor A^+_{Q_p}-lattices in N(V) satisfying the lattice versions of the conditions. LLZ print these as (1) free of rank d over O_E tensor A^+_{Q_p}; (2) 'the action of G_infinity preserves N(T)' (triviality modulo pi is NOT repeated in the lattice list); (3) the same q^{b-a} condition. [Corrected in review: the earlier text said 'the same three conditions'.]

Condition (3) involves the element q = phi(pi)/pi and the exponent b - a; both must be retained, and the weight interval [a,b] is part of the data
The identification N(V)/pi N(V) = D_cris(V) is stated for POSITIVE crystalline V (b = 0)

The filtration Fil^i N(V) = {x : phi(x) in q^i N(V)} is what makes N(V)/pi N(V) a filtered phi-module.

nodes.title: Two lattices with the same reduction have the same Wach module modulo p^n only above an explicit bound
nodes.statement: Let T_1 and T_2 be lattices in two crystalline representations with Hodge-Tate weights in [-r, 0] and suppose T_1/p^n = T_2/p^n with n satisfying p^{n-1}(p-1) >= r + 1. Then N_{T_1} and N_{T_2} have the same image in (A^+/p^n tensor T_i/p^n)^{H_F}. The bound is ESSENTIAL: counterexamples exist when p^{n-1}(p-1) <= r.

nodes.title: The family functor D_rig is fully faithful and exact but not essentially surjective onto etale objects
nodes.statement: Let A be a Q_p-affinoid algebra and V a finite projective A-module with a continuous A-linear G_K-action. There is a functorially associated (phi, Gamma_K)-module D_rig(V) over the relative Robba ring R_A(pi_K); the rule V -> D_rig(V) is fully faithful and exact and commutes with base change in A. It is NOT essentially surjective, even onto the etale objects. Moreover D_rig commutes with induction: D_rig(Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V) = Ind_L^K D_rig(V).

nodes.title: Perfectness, base change, Euler characteristic and Tate duality for families
nodes.statement: Let M be a (phi, Gamma_K)-module over R_A(pi_K) for A a Q_p-affinoid algebra. Then (1) C_psi(M) lies in D^-_perf(R_A^infinity(Gamma_K)) and in fact in D^{[0,2]}_perf; (2) C_{phi,gamma_K}(M) lies in D^{[0,2]}_perf(A), so the groups H^i_{phi,gamma_K}(M) are finite A-modules; (3) for any morphism A -> B of Q_p-affinoid algebras the canonical maps C_psi(M) derived-tensor R_B^infinity(Gamma_K) -> C_psi(M completed-tensor_A B) and C_{phi,gamma_K}(M) derived-tensor B -> C_{phi,gamma_K}(M completed-tensor_A B) are quasi-isomorphisms, so that for B FLAT over A the cohomology commutes with base change; (4) the Euler characteristic is -[K:Q_p] rank M in both settings; (5) Tate duality holds as a quasi-isomorphism C_{phi,gamma_K}(M) -> RHom_A(C_{phi,gamma_K}(M^*), A)[-2]; (6) M^{psi=1} is finitely presented over R_A^infinity(Gamma_K), H^0_psi(M) = 0, H^2_psi(M) is torsion, and H^1_psi(M) has generic rank [K:Q_p] rank M.
hypotheses: A is a Q_p-affinoid algebra; the coefficient ring for Iwasawa cohomology is R_A^infinity(Gamma_K), not the classical Iwasawa algebra
The base-change statement (3) is UNCONDITIONAL (no flatness needed) at the derived level; the untwisted isomorphism of cohomology groups needs B flat over A
The perfect amplitude [1,2] for C_psi does NOT follow, because H^1_psi(M) may have torsion; KPX state this explicitly in Theorem 4.4.6(3)
Theorem 4.4.5(2) and (3) are proved by reducing to a closed point and invoking Liu's Theorem 2.3.11, which itself requires A to be a finite extension of Q_p

Theorem 4.4.5(1): concentration in degrees 0,1,2 plus Lemma 4.1.4 gives a complex of finite projectives; flatness of the terms forces Coker(d^{-1}) projective.
Theorem 4.4.5(2),(3): check at one closed point per connected component, using Liu's Theorem 2.3.11(2),(3), then spread out by Lemma 4.1.5.

gaps.detail: THIS IS A FINDING ABOUT THE ATLAS, NOT ABOUT A SOURCE. Herr proves Theorem A (vanishing of H^i for i >= 3) in Sec. 2 from the phi-complex alone, which is PG.3's content.
